question: Will either Gulf Cup 27 semi-final on 3 October 2026 be decided by a penalty shootout?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Gulf Cup semi-finals under the current knockout format, editions 18-26 (2007-2025), n=18 matches across 9 editions. Four of those 18 semi-finals were decided by shootout (22% per match); four of the nine editions contained at least one (44%). The same 22% per-match rate holds over all 27 Gulf Cup knockout matches including finals, and a wider class (2023 AFC Asian Cup knockout stage, 3 shootouts in 16) sits in the same 19-25% band. Two near-independent matches at ~21% gives 1-(0.79)^2 = 38%, matching the edition-level count. Small downward shade: the cross-pairing (group winner vs other group's runner-up) builds in more quality asymmetry than a final, and hosts Saudi Arabia are a clear FIFA-ranking outlier in this field, so at least one tie is likelier to be a mismatch. Upward pull: Gulf semis are historically low-scoring and every Gulf Cup semi level after 90 has gone all the way to kicks (0 extra-time winners in 4). No market exists on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or any bookmaker - pairings are unknown until matchday 3 on 29-30 Sept - so there is no crowd anchor. The 27th edition's rules confirm extra time then shootout, matching the criterion's mechanism.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the match reports on the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup Wikipedia page (fallback: credible sources), NOT off official AGCFF bulletins. A shootout in EITHER of the two semi-finals resolves YES; a match settled in extra time counts as NOT a shootout. Only completed semi-finals count; if neither completes, annulled.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-10-03 (SF1 kickoff 18:00 UTC+3 = 15:00Z, SF2 21:30 UTC+3 = 18:30Z) -> resolution 2026-10-04T00:00:00Z, per the criteria text. As of Now 2026-09-22T17:40Z, 0% of the event window has elapsed; ~10.9 days to first kickoff.

STATUS QUO / STATE OF PLAY: Group stage had not kicked off as of Now (opening matches 23 Sept: Iraq v Oman, Saudi Arabia v Kuwait). Wikipedia group tables show zero matches played. Semi-final participants therefore unknown; matchday 3 concludes 29-30 Sept. Group A: Saudi Arabia (hosts, coach Giorgos Donis appointed April 2026), Iraq (Graham Arnold), Oman (Tarek Skiti), Kuwait (Helio Sousa). Group B: Qatar, UAE, Bahrain (defending champions), Yemen.

FORMAT RULE (Wikipedia, 27th ed.): 'In the knockout stage, extra time and penalty shoot-out are used to decide the winner if necessary' — i.e. 30 min ET first, then kicks. No source found indicating a straight-to-penalties rule.

BASE RATES — GULF CUP, knockout format introduced at the 18th edition (2007):
- Over all Gulf Cup SEMI-FINALS, editions 18-26 (n=18 matches): 4 decided by shootout. Source: per-edition Wikipedia knockout sections.
- Over all Gulf Cup KNOCKOUT matches incl. finals, editions 18-26 (n=27): 6 decided by shootout.
- Over Gulf Cup FINALS only, editions 18-26 (n=9): 2 by shootout (19th: Oman bt KSA 6-5 after 0-0 a.e.t.; 23rd: Oman bt UAE 5-4 after 0-0 a.e.t.); 5 of 9 finals reached extra time — finals run tighter than semis.
- CONDITIONAL, given a semi-final was level after 90 (n=4 of 18): all 4 went to kicks; zero extra-time winners in the semi-final sample. So the driver is almost entirely 'does it finish level after 90', not 'does ET break it'.
- Per-edition tally of semi-finals reaching a shootout: 18th 0/2, 19th 0/2, 20th 1/2 (Kuwait 2-2 Iraq a.e.t., Kuwait 5-4), 21st 1/2 (Iraq 1-1 Bahrain a.e.t., Iraq 4-2), 22nd 0/2, 23rd 1/2 (Iraq 0-0 UAE a.e.t., UAE 4-2), 24th 1/2 (Iraq 2-2 Bahrain a.e.t., Bahrain 5-3), 25th 0/2, 26th 0/2. No edition has ever had BOTH semi-finals go to kicks.
- Recent-window sub-rate: editions 25 (2023) and 26 (2024-25) — all four semi-finals decided in regulation (Iraq 2-1 Qatar; Oman 1-0 Bahrain; Oman 2-1 KSA; Bahrain 1-0 Kuwait).
- Iraq appears in 4 of the 4 historical semi-final shootouts; Bahrain in 2.

WIDER CLASS: 2023 AFC Asian Cup knockout stage (n=16, senior men's Asian knockout football with the same ET-then-kicks rule): 3 shootouts. 2019 AFC Asian Cup knockout stage (n=15): 2 shootouts, per the same Wikipedia series.

STRUCTURAL FEATURES CUTTING BOTH WAYS: (a) the pairings are winner-of-A v runner-up-of-B and vice versa, which builds in asymmetry a final does not have; (b) Saudi Arabia are hosts and the highest-FIFA-ranked side in the field, while Yemen are the field's clear tail; (c) Gulf Cup semi-finals are historically low-scoring — 1-0 is the single most common semi-final scoreline in the 18-26 sample; (d) two matches, so two independent draws at the event.

MARKETS: searched Polymarket, Manifold (direct site search), Kalshi and bookmaker listings for any contract on a Khaleeji 27 shootout or semi-final — none found on any venue. Bookmakers do not post 'to go to penalties' props for fixtures with unknown participants; pairings set 29-30 Sept.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: the official AGCFF/Khaleeji 27 competition regulations PDF (so the ET-then-kicks rule rests on Wikipedia plus the historical pattern that all four past semi-final shootouts followed a.e.t.); any published squad/injury news bearing on the knockout round; any prediction-market or bookmaker price on this event; a consolidated dataset of shootout frequency across all Gulf Cup editions (the tally above was compiled match-by-match from nine separate Wikipedia edition pages).
calls.reference_class: Arabian Gulf Cup semi-finals under the knockout format, editions 18-26 (2007-2025): 18 matches, 9 editions, each edition offering two independent chances at a shootout

calls.reasoning: Tournament starts 23 Sep 2026 and semi-finalists are unknown as of Now (2026-09-22), so this is essentially a base-rate question. Across the Gulf Cup's full knockout era (18th-26th editions, 2007-2025) 4 of 18 semi-finals (22%) were decided by kicks from the penalty mark; across all 27 knockout matches the rate is also 22% (9/27 level after 90, of which 6 went to kicks). Treating the two same-day semis as independent at p=0.22 gives 1-(0.78)^2 = 0.38, close to the directly observed 4/9 = 44% of editions with at least one semi shootout (in all four, exactly one of the two went to kicks). A same-region cross-check, the 2025 FIFA Arab Cup knockout stage, gives 2/8 = 25% per match. I trim slightly below the independence figure for the chance that one semi-final is a genuine mismatch (Yemen or Kuwait advancing against Saudi Arabia/Qatar/Iraq lowers that match's draw probability) and for the concavity of 2p-p^2 under uncertainty in p; the last two editions went 0-for-4 on semi shootouts, but 18 matches is the better anchor than 4. Extra time before kicks is confirmed for Khaleeji 27, so there is no 'straight to penalties' upside. No human prediction market or bookmaker line on this proposition was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, or via general search.

STATUS QUO: no shootout — both semi-finals decided in regulation or extra time (the NO branch covers two of the three possible endings per match).

EVIDENCE (source + date):
- Tournament runs 23 Sep - 6 Oct 2026 in Jeddah; Group A = Saudi Arabia (hosts), Iraq, Oman, Kuwait; Group B = Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Yemen. Group matchday 3 ends 29-30 Sep, so pairings are unknown as of 22 Sep 2026. (Wikipedia 27th Arabian Gulf Cup, AFP schedule 21 Sep 2026)

- Bahrain are defending champions (26th edition, Jan 2025). Coaches: Saudi Arabia - Giorgos Donis (appointed Apr 2026); Iraq - Graham Arnold; Oman - Tarek Skiti; Kuwait - Helio Sousa. (UrduPoint, 22 Sep 2026)
- Qatar's Assim Madibo carries a suspension affecting availability during the tournament. (Wikipedia 27th Arabian Gulf Cup)
- Edition-by-edition semi-final endings, knockout era (all Wikipedia edition pages, retrieved 22 Sep 2026): 18th/2007 Oman 1-0 Bahrain, UAE 1-0 KSA (both regulation). 19th/2009 Oman 1-0 Qatar, KSA 1-0 Kuwait (both regulation). 20th/2010 Kuwait 2-2 Iraq a.e.t., Kuwait won 5-4 on kicks; KSA 1-0 UAE. 21st/2013 UAE 1-0 Kuwait; Iraq 1-1 Bahrain a.e.t., Iraq won 4-2 on kicks. 22nd/2014 Qatar 3-1 Oman, KSA 3-2 UAE (both regulation). 23rd/2017-18 Oman 1-0 Bahrain; Iraq 0-0 UAE a.e.t., UAE won 4-2 on kicks. 24th/2019 Iraq 2-2 Bahrain a.e.t., Bahrain won 5-3 on kicks; KSA 1-0 Qatar. 25th/2023 Iraq 2-1 Qatar, Oman 1-0 Bahrain (both regulation). 26th/2024-25 Oman 2-1 KSA, Bahrain 1-0 Kuwait (both regulation).
- Gulf Cup FINALS, same era: 2007 regulation; 2009 0-0 a.e.t., kicks; 2010 extra-time goal (93'); 2013 extra-time goal (107'); 2014 regulation; 2017-18 0-0 a.e.t., kicks; 2019 regulation; 2023 3-2 a.e.t. (extra-time goals); 2024-25 regulation.
- 2025 FIFA Arab Cup knockout stage (Dec 2025, Qatar; overlapping Gulf teams): QF Morocco 1-0 Syria, Palestine 1-2 KSA a.e.t., Jordan 1-0 Iraq, Algeria 1-1 UAE a.e.t. decided on kicks 7-6; SF Morocco 3-0 UAE, KSA 0-1 Jordan; third place Algeria 1-1 KSA a.e.t. decided on kicks; final Jordan 2-0 Morocco. (Wikipedia)
- Pre-18th-edition Gulf Cups used a round-robin format with no knockout semi-finals, so the knockout sample starts in 2007.

BASE RATES (with the class each is computed over):
- Over all 18 Gulf Cup semi-finals 2007-2025: 4 decided by kicks.
- Over the 9 editions (unit = a PAIR of same-day semis): 4 editions had at least one semi go to kicks; in all four, exactly one of the two did (never both, never more than one per edition).
- Over all 27 Gulf Cup knockout matches 2007-2025 (18 semis + 9 finals): 6 decided by kicks; 9 were level after 90 minutes; of those 9, 6 reached kicks and 3 were settled by an extra-time goal.
- Over the 9 Gulf Cup finals only: 2 decided by kicks.
- Over the 8 knockout matches of the 2025 FIFA Arab Cup: 2 decided by kicks; 3 went to extra time.
- Conditional note: no separate rate is available for semi-finals involving a large FIFA-ranking gap vs. a close one — the 18-match sample is too small to split, but approximate current FIFA ranks are Qatar ~53, Iraq ~58, Saudi Arabia ~60, UAE ~65, Oman ~80, Bahrain ~85, Kuwait ~135, Yemen ~160, so the two groups differ in how lopsided a qualifier pair could be.

EVIDENCE POINTING BOTH WAYS:
- Toward a shootout: Gulf Cup knockouts are low-scoring (seven of the nine editions' semi-final pairs contain at least one 1-0 or 0-0 scoreline); a third of all knockout matches in the era were level after 90; six of the eight teams sit within ~35 FIFA ranking places of each other; single-leg semis with regional-rivalry stakes and a compressed group stage (matchday 3 on 29-30 Sep, semis 3 Oct, i.e. 3-4 days' rest).
- Against a shootout: Group B contains Yemen (~160) and Group A contains Kuwait (~135), so one semi-final could be a lopsided pairing; in three of the last four editions' semi-final pairs both matches finished inside 90 minutes; the last two editions (2023, 2024-25) produced four semi-finals with no extra time at all; host Saudi Arabia plays in front of a home crowd, which historically correlates with decisive rather than level results in this competition.

MARKETS: searched Polymarket, Manifold (harness title search), Kalshi and general bookmaker coverage for a contract on a Gulf Cup semi-final shootout — none found. Only World Cup 2026 penalty-shootout-count contracts exist, which are a different tournament and a different resolution rule.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: an official GFF regulations PDF for Khaleeji 27 confirming extra-time length and shootout procedure (only the Wikipedia statement that extra time and kicks are used); any published bookmaker draw-after-90 line for the semi-finals; a reliable breakdown of AFC Asian Cup 2023 knockout endings (the retrieved summary of that page was internally inconsistent and is NOT relied on here); any Gulf Cup shootout rate conditioned on ranking gap.
calls.reference_class: Arabian Gulf Cup semi-finals in the knockout era (18th-26th editions, 2007-2025): 18 matches / 9 editions, each edition being a pair of same-day semi-finals with extra time then kicks

calls.reasoning: Two independent single-leg knockout matches, each needing to be level after 90 AND level after extra time. Empirical per-match shootout rate in comparable senior knockout football is ~20% (World Cup 35/161 since 1982; AFC Asian Cup 2019+2023 6/30), and Gulf Cup's own knockout era runs slightly hotter at 4/18 (22%) with 3/12 semi-finals specifically. Decomposed: ~30% level after 90 in cautious knockout play x ~65% of extra times ending level = ~0.20 per match; 1-(0.80)^2 = 0.36 for at least one of two. Small upward pull from Gulf Cup's low-scoring parity and a congested schedule in Jeddah heat; small downward pull from likely strength mismatch in at least one pairing (hosts Saudi Arabia vs a Group B runner-up) and from positive correlation between two same-day matches. No prediction market or bookmaker price found for this contract, so no crowd anchor. The semi-finalists are not yet known (group stage starts 23 Sep), so no team-specific information is available to move off the reference class.

A match won by a goal in extra time counts as NOT a shootout. Abandoned/forfeited semi-finals are excluded; if neither completes, annulment.

EVENT WINDOW: 3 October 2026, SF1 at 18:00 UTC+3 and SF2 at 21:30 UTC+3 in Jeddah, per the criteria; as of 2026-09-22T17:40Z, 0% elapsed (the window has not opened; ~10.9 days out). Group stage runs 23-30 September 2026; semi-final pairings are unknown at this timestamp.

RULES: Wikipedia's 27th Arabian Gulf Cup page states 'In the knockout stage, extra time and penalty shoot-out are used to decide the winner if necessary' — identical wording to the 26th edition page. No evidence found of a straight-to-penalties (no extra time) rule in this edition.

BASE RATES FOUND:
- Gulf Cup semi-finals, knockout era (editions 21-26, 2013-2025, n=12 matches): 3 decided by shootout. Class = all Gulf Cup semi-finals since the group+knockout format began. (Wikipedia edition pages.)
- Gulf Cup editions with at least one semi-final shootout: 3 of 6 (21st 2013, 23rd 2018, 24th 2019 yes; 22nd 2014, 25th 2023, 26th 2024-25 no). Class = editions, i.e. the exact 'at least one of two' unit.
- Gulf Cup all knockout matches since 2013 (semis + finals, n=18): 6 level after 90 minutes; 4 of those 6 reached a shootout. Conditional rate of shootout given level after 90 ≈ 2 in 3. (Wikipedia edition pages.)
- FIFA World Cup: ~35 shootouts across ~161 knockout matches 1982-2022, i.e. roughly 1 in 5 knockout matches; 13 of the 35 came in 2014-2022. Class = all WC knockout matches. (Opta Analyst; sports-king almanac.)
- AFC Asian Cup knockout rounds 2019 + 2023 combined: 6 shootouts in 30 knockout matches. Class = continental senior knockout matches in Asia. (Tournament results.)
- Arab Cup 2021 knockout: 1 shootout in 7 knockout matches, but 3 of 7 needed extra time. Class = Arab regional senior knockout.

MATCH-BY-MATCH GULF CUP SEMI-FINAL RECORD:
- 21st (2013, Bahrain): UAE 1-0 Kuwait (90'); Iraq 1-1 Bahrain AET, Iraq 4-2 on pens.
- 22nd (2014, Riyadh): Qatar 3-1 Oman; Saudi Arabia 3-2 UAE. Both in regulation.
- 23rd (2017-18, Kuwait): Oman 1-0 Bahrain; Iraq 0-0 UAE AET, UAE 4-2 on pens. (Final also went 0-0 AET to pens, Oman 5-4.)
- 24th (2019, Qatar): Iraq 2-2 Bahrain AET, Bahrain 5-3 on pens; Saudi Arabia 1-0 Qatar.
- 25th (2023, Basra): Iraq 2-1 Qatar; Bahrain 0-1 Oman. Both in regulation. (Final Iraq 3-2 Oman AET, goal in 120+2.)
- 26th (2024-25, Kuwait): Oman 2-1 Saudi Arabia; Bahrain 1-0 Kuwait. Both in regulation; final Bahrain 2-1 Oman in regulation.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: in the absence of a shootout in either match, the question resolves NO; the default path for any single knockout match is a decision inside 90 minutes.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD MORE DRAWS/SHOOTOUTS: Gulf Cup is historically tight and low-scoring, with three of the last six finals needing extra time or penalties; the eight entrants cluster within a narrow FIFA-ranking band (Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, UAE, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait), with Yemen the clear outlier; 23-30 September to 3 October is a compressed schedule; the tournament falls outside a FIFA international window (Sept window closed ~8 Sept, next opens ~5 Oct), so European- and some club-based players may be absent, flattening squad-quality gaps; Jeddah early-October heat suppresses tempo and scoring.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD FEWER: the crossover format (Group A winner vs Group B runner-up) systematically pairs a stronger side against a weaker one rather than seeding equals together; hosts Saudi Arabia have home advantage and a large crowd at King Abdullah Sports City; the last two editions (2023, 2024-25) produced four straight semi-finals settled in regulation; the broader cross-tournament rate for single knockout matches (World Cup, Asian Cup) sits below the Gulf Cup's own small-sample semi-final rate, which suggests some of the Gulf figure is noise.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: any prediction-market or bookmaker contract on 'Gulf Cup 27 semi-final decided by penalties' — Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold and general odds searches returned nothing for this tournament (harness title search on Polymarket/Manifold also returned no candidate); the official GFF/AGCFF competition regulations PDF specifying the knockout tie-break wording for this edition (only the Wikipedia restatement was found); any published per-competition shootout-frequency dataset covering the Gulf Cup specifically; any announcement of rule variation (e.g. golden goal, no extra time) for Khaleeji 27.
calls.reference_class: Single-leg semi-finals/knockout matches in senior Gulf Cup and comparable Asian/Arab regional tournaments, where ET then penalties applies

calls.reasoning: Semi-finalists are unknown as of 2026-09-22 (group stage opens 23 Sept, matchday 3 ends 29-30 Sept), so this is a pure base-rate question with no team-specific information. Gulf Cup knockout era 2007-2025: 4 of 18 semi-finals decided by kicks (22%); same 22% across all 27 knockout matches; 4 of 9 editions had at least one semi go to kicks, never both. Wider comparable classes run slightly cooler - World Cup 35/161 (21.7%), AFC Asian Cup 2019+2023 6/30 (20%), 2025 Arab Cup 2/8 - so I shrink the Gulf figure toward ~0.20 per match rather than treating it as genuinely hotter. Two matches at 0.20 gives 1-(0.80)^2 = 0.36; I take a small further discount for positive correlation between two same-day matches sharing heat, schedule congestion and tournament tempo, and for a modest chance one tie is a genuine mismatch (Yemen ~160 or Kuwait ~135 advancing). Format is confirmed extra time then kicks, so there is no straight-to-penalties upside. No human market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or any bookmaker - books do not post penalty props for fixtures with unknown participants - so there is no crowd anchor.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes were narrow (runs at 0.36/0.36/0.37). FACTUAL: (a) Run 3 dated the knockout format to 2013 and used n=12 semis / 3 shootouts; Runs 1 and 2 independently reconstructed the 18th (2007), 19th (2009) and 20th (2010) semi-finals with matching scorelines including the 20th-edition shootout (Kuwait 2-2 Iraq a.e.t., 5-4 on kicks). Two independent match-level reconstructions beat one unsourced window, so I carry n=18 / 4 shootouts = 22%; Run 3's figure is a subset, not a contradiction. (b) The conditional 'level after 90 -> kicks' rates (4/4 in semis per Run 1; 6/9 across all knockout matches per Run 2, the three extra-time winners all being finals) are the same data sliced differently, not a conflict - but 4/4 is a four-case sample and I do not treat it as a real 100%; I use the directly observed per-match shootout rate instead, which already embeds the extra-time path and needs no decomposition. (c) All three runs, plus the harness title search, found no market on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or any bookmaker; settled as no crowd anchor. (d) None of the three could retrieve the official GFF/AGCFF regulations PDF, so the extra-time-then-kicks rule rests on Wikipedia plus the fact that all four historical semi-final shootouts followed a.e.t. That gap is genuinely unsettled here (no web access this run) but is low-stakes. JUDGMENT: Run 2's downward 'concavity of 2p-p^2' adjustment is directionally wrong - with p1+p2 fixed, spread raises P(at least one) (0.1/0.3 -> 0.37 vs 0.2/0.2 -> 0.36) - so a mismatch only helps the NO side by lowering the mean p, which is a modest effect given only Yemen and Kuwait are real tails and each must beat two stronger sides to reach a semi. On the 0-for-4 last two editions I side with Runs 1 and 2: four matches is noise against eighteen. Net: per-match ~0.20-0.21 after shrinking the Gulf-specific 22% toward the wider ~20% class, two draws, small discount for same-day correlation and mismatch, small credit for Jeddah heat and off-FIFA-window squads. 0.35 - marginally below all three members because the shrinkage toward the wider class is the one adjustment none of them applied in full.

disagreements.verdict: Settled for 2007: Runs 1 and 2 independently list the 18th/19th/20th-edition semi-final scorelines, including the 20th-edition shootout Run 3 omits. Base rate = 4/18 = 22%.

disagreements.claim: Given a semi-final is level after 90, the probability it reaches kicks is 100% (4/4, Run 1) vs ~2/3 (6/9, Run 2) vs ~65% (Run 3).
disagreements.verdict: Same data, different slices - no real conflict. The 4/4 semi-final figure is a four-case sample; I sidestep it by using the directly observed per-match shootout rate, which already incorporates extra-time outcomes.

disagreements.claim: A human market or bookmaker line exists on this proposition.
disagreements.verdict: Settled NO. All three runs plus the harness search found nothing on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers; participants are unknown until 29-30 Sept, and books do not post penalty props for unknown fixtures.

Wikipedia's wording plus all four historical Gulf Cup semi shootouts following a.e.t. make the standard rule near-certain, and the residual uncertainty would push the estimate up, not down.

disagreements.claim: Whether the Gulf Cup's own 22% or the wider senior-knockout ~20% is the better per-match anchor.
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks this tie - 4 events cannot distinguish 20% from 22%. I shrink toward the wider class (World Cup 21.7%, Asian Cup 20%), which is the bet I would take and the main reason my number sits just below all three runs.
